title: OpenCl compiling issue
body: Hi, I'm trying to compile llama.cpp using my OpenCL drivers on a Samsung S10+ with Termux. Running make with LLAMA_CLBLAST=1 fails because ggml-opencl.cpp cannot find clblast.h. I tried replacing <clblast.h> with ocl_icd.h because my OpenCL files are under /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/include, but the next build fails in ggml-opencl.cpp with an undeclared identifier 'clblast'.

symptoms_visible: Building with LLAMA_CLBLAST=1 first fails with 'clblast.h file not found'. After I replace that header with ocl_icd.h, ggml-opencl.cpp fails with "use of undeclared identifier 'clblast'".
N0.label: N0 CLBlast header build failure

symptoms_visible: The CMake build completes and I can run main from the build/bin directory, but startup does not show BLAS = 1 or an OpenCL platform and device.
N1_x.label: N1_x generic CMake build without CLBlast

symptoms_visible: Configuring with -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON reports 'CLBlast not found' and says it cannot find CLBlastConfig.cmake or clblast-config.cmake.
N2.label: N2 CMake cannot locate CLBlast package

symptoms_visible: CLBlast builds, but make install tries to create /usr/local/lib and stops with 'Maybe need administrative privileges'. Llama.cpp still reports that CLBlast is not found.
N3_x.label: N3_x CLBlast installed with wrong CMake prefix setting

symptoms_visible: After installing CLBlast under the Termux prefix, llama.cpp finds CLBlast and builds successfully. Running main through clvk then prints OpenCL kernel errors about unsupported 16-bit and 8-bit storage and scalar alignment.
N4.label: N4 CLBlast build succeeds but clvk runtime fails

symptoms_visible: Main still prints the OpenCL kernel errors when it uses clvk, while my manually built clinfo can see the phone's native Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 Adreno 640 device.
N5.label: N5 native Qualcomm OpenCL measured

symptoms_visible: After removing clvk, clinfo reports zero platforms and main stops with clGetPlatformIDs error -1001. The phone's libOpenCL.so is under the Android vendor lib64 directory, not the Termux lib directory.
N5_x.label: N5_x native OpenCL not found through default runtime path

symptoms_visible: Llama.cpp builds with CLBlast enabled and main starts with GPU acceleration when I launch it with the vendor and Termux library directories in LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
N_terminal.label: terminal CLBlast GPU execution working

solution.intent: Switch from make to a generic CMake build and run main from the build/bin directory.
solution.concrete_example: Configure and build with CMake, then run ./main from the bin subdirectory of the build directory.

edges.comment: Reporter c2-c4 on the reporter's Samsung/Termux system: a generic CMake build produced a runnable main under build/bin, but CLBlast was not compiled in, so this did not resolve the requested OpenCL build.

solution.intent: Enable the CLBlast backend explicitly during CMake configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Reconfigure with cmake -B build -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON, then rebuild and check startup for the selected OpenCL platform and device.

edges.comment: Participant1 c5 and reporter c6, all on the reporter's system: enabling LLAMA_CLBLAST exposed the next concrete problem, namely that no installed CLBlast package configuration could be found.

solution.intent: Treat CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH as CLBlast's installation destination while building CLBlast.
solution.concrete_example: Configure CLBlast with -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr, build it, and run make install.

edges.comment: Reporter c10 on the reporter's system: CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH was used where CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX was needed. CLBlast built but make install still targeted /usr/local/lib and failed for lack of permission.

solution.intent: Install a real CLBlast build into the writable Termux prefix, then configure a fresh llama.cpp build with CLBlast enabled.
solution.concrete_example: In the CLBlast build directory run cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr, then make install. Use a fresh llama.cpp source/build directory and configure it with cmake -B build -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON.

edges.comment: Participant1 c11 and reporter c12 on the reporter's system: correcting CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX allowed CLBlast to install and llama.cpp to find and compile the backend. The later runtime failure is a separate driver-discovery/kernel issue.

question_patterns: Can you check whether the phone exposes a native OpenCL platform by compiling and running clinfo yourself?
What platform and device does a manually built clinfo report on the phone?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I manually built clinfo. It reports one platform, 'QUALCOMM Snapdragon(TM)', with OpenCL 2.0 and one GPU device, 'QUALCOMM Adreno(TM) 640'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My manually built clinfo also reports zero platforms and no OpenCL devices.
It reports the same Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 platform but with a slightly different driver build string.

question_patterns: What capabilities does that native clinfo output list for half-precision values?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The native Qualcomm output lists a preferred and native half vector size of 1 and shows cl_khr_fp16 half-precision support.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The maximum work-group size is different, but the same native platform and cl_khr_fp16 support are present.

edges.comment: Participant3 c33-c36 and reporter c35 on the reporter's Samsung phone: manually built clinfo establishes that the native Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 platform exists and advertises cl_khr_fp16. This measurement walks back the earlier conclusion that the phone's OpenCL implementation is inherently incompatible due to missing half precision.

solution.intent: Remove clvk and expect the default Termux ICD setup to discover the phone's native OpenCL driver without additional runtime-path configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Uninstall clvk, rebuild against the Termux OpenCL loader, and run main normally so it uses the phone's native OpenCL implementation.

edges.comment: Reporter c20 and c37-c41 on the reporter's phone: removing clvk and relying on default ICD discovery did not expose the native Qualcomm platform to main. The Termux loader returned no platform while the vendor OpenCL library existed outside the Termux library directory.

solution.intent: Use a clean Termux environment, install the OpenCL loader and headers, build and install CLBlast under the Termux prefix, build llama.cpp with CLBlast enabled, and expose both the Android vendor and Termux library directories when launching main.
solution.concrete_example: Install opencl-headers, opencl-clhpp, ocl-icd and clinfo. Build CLBlast with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DTUNERS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr, run make install, then build llama.cpp with cmake -B build -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON. Launch from build/bin with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:$PREFIX/lib ./main and confirm that the OpenCL platform/device is selected.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the contrast between native clinfo seeing the Qualcomm platform, the default Termux run returning clGetPlatformIDs -1001, and libOpenCL.so existing under the Android vendor directory. Concluding that the launch environment must expose /vendor/lib64 to the Termux-linked executable is the diagnostic inference.

edges.comment: Reporter c42 gives the reporter's confirmed resolution on the Samsung S10+: a fresh Termux dependency setup, CLBlast installed with CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, llama.cpp built with LLAMA_CLBLAST, and main launched with /vendor/lib64 plus $PREFIX/lib in LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

solution.intent: Resolve the Termux build end to end by restoring the real CLBlast header, installing CLBlast into the Termux prefix, enabling it in a clean CMake build, and launching with the Android vendor library path available.
solution.concrete_example: Do not substitute ocl_icd.h for clblast.h. From a clean Termux setup, install the OpenCL headers and ICD loader, build and install CLBlast under /data/data/com.termux/files/usr, configure llama.cpp with -DLLAMA_CLBLAST=ON, and run build/bin/main with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:$PREFIX/lib. Verify that startup identifies the OpenCL platform and device.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut states the thread's eventual working Termux recipe directly. It skips the failed generic CMake build, wrong installation-prefix attempt, clvk detour, and native-driver discovery probes.

edges.comment: Shortcut to the reporter's c42 confirmed recipe, provided so an agent that gives the complete correct setup immediately can match without reproducing the thread's failed attempts.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the initial build problem correctly: OpenCL headers or ocl_icd.h are not substitutes for the missing CLBlast API; an actual CLBlast installation and its CMake package files are required.
Must use CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX, not CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH, to install CLBlast into the writable Termux prefix, then configure a clean llama.cpp build with LLAMA_CLBLAST enabled.

Must account for the final runtime issue: the phone's native Qualcomm OpenCL platform exists, but the Termux-linked executable needs the Android vendor library directory exposed at launch alongside the Termux library directory.
Must not conclude that the device is incompatible merely because clvk reports storage or half-related kernel errors; native clinfo reports Qualcomm OpenCL 2.0 with cl_khr_fp16 support.
Must not recommend replacing clblast.h with ocl_icd.h, pointing CLBlast_DIR at an include directory, or using CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH as CLBlast's installation destination.
Must ask the user to verify that main starts, identifies an OpenCL platform/device, and actually runs with GPU acceleration before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Persistent but relatively inexperienced Termux user who can clone repositories, run CMake and make commands, edit configuration files, rebuild tools, and paste detailed compiler or runtime output, but needs explicit guidance about headers, package discovery, installation prefixes, ICD loaders, and library paths.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and highly cooperative; reports exact commands and long logs, openly says when concepts are unclear, and follows up with a tested step-by-step resolution for other users.
